clue.text: Price a way for Navarrois clown

parts.note: the price of something is what it costs
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone haggles over the fee for a jester at the court of Navarre.
explanation.walkthrough: The clown is the one in Love's Labour's Lost, set at the court of the King of Navarre.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare names his fool in the Navarre comedy by this word, which is also an old apple and slang for the head.

clue.text: Beholden, say, if Salinger's

parts.note: split 'Beholden' as 'Be Holden': to be Salinger's Holden is to bear his teenage narrator's surname

explanation.surface: Someone owes a debt of gratitude to the author of The Catcher in the Rye.
explanation.definitionFit: Holden, narrator of The Catcher in the Rye, carries this family name.

clue.text: Hailstorm in SWI, language ensues

indicators.note: the stirred-up letters are placed inside the letters SWI

parts.note: the word hail is stormed, its letters thrown about, giving AHIL

explanation.surface: A hailstorm strikes the southwest, and some talk follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' is fused to 'Hail' in one word, so the anagram signal hides inside its own fodder; the result goes into SWI, standing for the letters as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bantu tongue spoken widely across East Africa, a lingua franca of Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Creator of the flower of detectives

definitions.text: Creator of the flower of detectives

parts.words: Creator of the flower of detectives
parts.note: the flower is the campion, so this is whoever invented the sleuth Albert Campion, not the pick of the force

explanation.surface: A tribute to whoever trained the finest of all investigators.
explanation.definitionFit: Margery of that surname wrote the Albert Campion mysteries, and campion is a wild flower.

clue.text: Valley of romantic novelist

definitions.meaning: Ethel M. of that name, popular writer of romances early in the twentieth century

explanation.definitionFit: A small wooded vale shares its name with Ethel M., the bestselling author of love stories.

clue.text: Somerset author

parts.note: not a writer from the English county but one whose first name was Somerset

explanation.surface: A writer from the West Country county.
explanation.definitionFit: W. Somerset of this surname wrote Of Human Bondage and The Moon and Sixpence.

clue.text: Entertaining storyteller, graduate at university, passing in French

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
the French word for passing is passant

explanation.surface: A lively raconteur who took a degree and then passed through a French course.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy de, the nineteenth-century French writer, is famed for his short tales such as Boule de Suif.

clue.text: The one in Sheridan's book was villainous

definitions.text: The one in Sheridan's book was villainous

parts.words: The one in Sheridan's book was villainous
parts.note: Sheridan is not the playwright but Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu, whose novel names a wicked relative, Silas, in its title

explanation.surface: A remark that a character in a Sheridan work was a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Fanu's novel Uncle Silas is about a sinister relative, the brother of the heroine's father.

clue.text: "dark, and smells of cheese!" (R. S. Surtees)

definitions.text: "dark, and smells of cheese!" (R. S. Surtees)

parts.words: "dark, and smells of cheese!" (R. S. Surtees)
parts.note: fill in the missing opening word of Jorrocks's exclamation in Surtees, an intensifier meaning devilishly

explanation.surface: A quotation from Surtees with its first word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Jorrocks, in Handley Cross, peers out of bed and says it is very dark and smells of cheese; the gap takes his oath-like intensifier.
explanation.definitionFit: The word used here is an adverb meaning extremely, literally infernal.

clue.text: Ran into first real exception in rhythm mic arrangement

parts.note: to run into someone is to meet them, past tense met

indicators.note: the opening letters of the words real and exception are taken

explanation.surface: Someone bumped into a rare exception while arranging a beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Metre is the measured pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables in verse.

clue.text: Early dramatist in bud all the time

indicators.note: the dramatist's name is found inside the run of words bud all the time

explanation.surface: An early playwright is still in bud, never blooming.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicholas of this name wrote Ralph Roister Doister, among the first English comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas, Tudor schoolmaster, wrote one of the earliest English stage comedies.

clue.text: Legendary knight finds uncle a new sales item

indicators.note: the letters of uncle and a are made new, rearranged

parts.note: a lot is an item put up at an auction sale

explanation.surface: An Arthurian hero discovers that his uncle is a fresh auction piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal on 'uncle a'; the knight's name is the old spelling found in Malory and Tennyson's sources.
explanation.definitionFit: An old spelling of the name of Arthur's greatest Round Table champion, Guinevere's lover.

clue.text: Anita Brookner's was from England

parts.note: fills the title of Brookner's 1987 novel, which names a companion who is English

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a Brookner character hailed from England.
explanation.definitionFit: Brookner's novel A ___ from England, so the word means a companion or pal.

clue.text: Eli and Dante involved in indication of day of issue

indicators.note: the letters of the two names are tangled, involved together, and rearranged

explanation.surface: Two figures, a biblical priest and an Italian poet, get caught up in the date-stamping of a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: The line at the top of a newspaper report stating where and when it was filed.

clue.text: Architectural feature mentioned in plain account

indicators.note: said out loud, so the words for plain account are heard

parts.note: plain means clear, an account is a story

explanation.surface: A building detail described in an unadorned report.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper storey of a church nave, pierced by windows that light the interior.

clue.text: Cut out initial hesitation from one of the Sitwells

parts.note: to edit text is to cut parts out of it

indicators.note: the first letter of the word hesitation

explanation.surface: Remove a stammered pause from something one of the literary Sitwells said.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Edith, poet of Façade, was the eldest of the three literary Sitwell siblings.

clue.text: Chabrol does

parts.note: not a verb: does are female deer, and in French they give the title of a 1968 film by Claude Chabrol

explanation.surface: A remark about what the French director gets up to.
explanation.definitionFit: Chabrol's film title is French for female deer, with the plural article.

clue.text: Graves's revelation of part of confession by Hamlet's 6?

definitions.text: Graves's revelation of part of confession by Hamlet's 6?

parts.words: Graves's revelation of part of confession by Hamlet's 6?
parts.note: 6 is the relative in 6-down, so Hamlet's father's brother, the usurping king, opening a confession in the first person; Robert Graves used those words as a title

explanation.surface: A gravedigger's disclosure of a confession linked to Hamlet's family.
explanation.walkthrough: Graves looks like the churchyard of Hamlet's gravediggers; it is Robert Graves, author of the novel about the Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Graves's novel is written as the emperor's own memoir, starting with his name.

clue.text: Gardener-poet: he is involved with sonnets

indicators.note: the letters of he and sonnets are mixed up together, involved with each other

explanation.surface: A gardening poet is caught up with writing fourteen-line verses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is involved with' scrambles HE and SONNETS.
explanation.definitionFit: William, eighteenth-century poet, created the celebrated landscape garden at The Leasowes.

clue.text: Italian stories of the French doctor of Cronin

parts.note: de is French for of
Dr Cameron is the senior doctor in A. J. Cronin's Dr Finlay stories

explanation.surface: A collection of Italian tales drawn from a French physician created by Cronin.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's fourteenth-century collection of a hundred tales told over ten days.

clue.text: Dickens barrister holding ring in satirical drawing

indicators.note: one word is placed around another, holding it inside

parts.note: Sydney Carton is the dissolute barrister in A Tale of Two Cities
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A Dickensian lawyer clutches a ring in a lampoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic or satirical sketch in a newspaper, mocking public figures.

clue.text: Secondary school French

parts.note: not language lessons but the French name for a state secondary school

explanation.surface: A subject on the curriculum: French at secondary level.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term for a state high school preparing pupils for the baccalauréat.

clue.text: Church doctor a student, with love for dulcimer

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
L is the learner plate sign
love is zero in tennis, shaped O

explanation.surface: A church doctor and a student swap affection for a stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word once named the hammered dulcimer before it came to mean the harpsichord.

clue.text: Somnolent guest, could be awakened at a pinch

definitions.text: Somnolent guest, could be awakened at a pinch

parts.words: Somnolent guest, could be awakened at a pinch
parts.note: the drowsy creature at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice, roused when pinched

explanation.surface: A sleepy visitor who can be roused if absolutely necessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at a pinch' reads as 'if need be', but in Alice the Hatter and Hare literally pinch the sleeper awake.
explanation.definitionFit: The sleepy rodent at the tea party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

clue.text: Fiction writer introduces dramatic yarns, some oddly naturalistic

indicators.note: the introducing letters, the first of each of the words that follow, are taken

explanation.surface: A novelist brings in theatrical tales, some strangely true to life.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname borne by a novelist, the person the clue identifies as a writer of fiction.

clue.text: Minor guest shows keyboard instrument in France

indicators.note: the French word shows itself inside the words minor guest

explanation.surface: A lesser visitor plays an instrument while in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for organ, the keyboard instrument of churches.

clue.text: Whose bell strikes ten in Aurora Leigh?

definitions.text: Whose bell strikes ten in Aurora Leigh?

parts.words: Whose bell strikes ten in Aurora Leigh?
parts.note: in Barrett Browning's poem, set partly in Florence, the hour is rung by the cathedral; the plural is asked for because ten is struck on more than one

explanation.surface: A question about which church tower chimes ten in Barrett Browning's verse novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian cathedrals, whose bells ring out the hours over the cities of Aurora Leigh.

clue.text: Rachel's sister heard name of English king

indicators.note: the name is spoken out loud and only its sound counts

parts.note: Lear is the legendary king of ancient Britain in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Rachel's sister heard the name of an old British ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the final r of the king's name is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Laban's elder daughter, whom Jacob married before her younger sister.

clue.text: It's Owen's go, so unexpectedly to define bird in fiction…

indicators.note: the letters of Owen's go so are rearranged in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Owen takes his turn and surprisingly defines a fictional bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' shuffles OWENS, GO and SO into the bird of Paul Gallico's novella.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Gallico's novella of Dunkirk takes its title from a white wild goose of the Arctic.

clue.text: … so give him a go to include Nicholas Mosley's

indicators.note: the words him a go include the hidden title word within them

explanation.surface: Someone urges another to let him have a turn, including a Mosley novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries 'bird in fiction' over: Mosley's novel is Imago Bird, so the def needs its missing second word.
explanation.definitionFit: The first word of Nicholas Mosley's 1980 novel title, also the adult stage of an insect.

clue.text: Its occupants apparently in jeopardy in Boyd book

definitions.text: Its occupants apparently in jeopardy in Boyd book

parts.words: Its occupants apparently in jeopardy in Boyd book
parts.note: describes a convent whose sisters seem to be at risk in a novel by Boyd

explanation.surface: A building whose residents seem to be in danger in a Boyd novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent, a house where women of a religious order live.

clue.text: Noise he made indicating Priam's sister

indicators.note: the letters of noise and he are made into a new word

explanation.surface: A man made a racket to point to the sister of Troy's king.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the Trojan princess rescued by Heracles from a sea monster, sibling of Troy's king.
